header.question: Is model evaluation enough on its own to assess extreme risks from AI?

events.text: Start with the paper that argues for evaluations and see what it claims for them. Then look for the limits it admits, and whether NIST treats risk measurement as settled.
Page 6 says evaluation is one tool among several. The paper has a limitations section; read it.

answer.text:
No. The paper that makes the case for evaluations says model evaluation is “not the only tool available for AI risk assessment” , though it is “one of the main tools we have for AI risk assessment” . Its limitations section goes further and calls evaluation “a necessary and sufficient strategy for identifying and mitigating extreme risks” .

NIST's AI Risk Management Framework agrees that measurement is hard: risks that are not well understood are “difficult to measure quantitatively or qualitatively” , and it lists the lack of reliable metrics among the open challenges .
